stem.text: Carbon dioxide is continually produced by respiring cells. It diffuses into red blood cells and dissociates into hydrogen ions ($\text{H}^{+}$) and hydrogen carbonate ions ($\text{HCO}_3^{-}$). $\text{HCO}_3^{-}$ then diffuses out of the cell in exchange for chloride ions ($\text{Cl}^{-}$) in the chloride shift.
What is the importance of the chloride shift?

A.text: It helps to maintain a neutral pH in the red blood cell by acting as a buffer.

B.text: It maintains a balance of positive and negative charge between the cell and the plasma.

C.text: It causes the oxygen dissociation curve to shift to the left, releasing more oxygen.

D.text: It prevents carbon dioxide combining with haemoglobin, allowing haemoglobin to combine with oxygen.
